---
title: "Typography"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8.8, fig.height = 4.4, dpi = 100,
  fig.retina = 2, dev = "ragg_png", out.width = "100%"
)
options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")
library(ggplot2)
library(gglaplot2)
```

The design system describes type by role rather than by size. A role names
the job a piece of text does and carries the size, weight and line height
that job needs. The chart set has seven roles, and `theme_gla()` sets its
text from them.

```{r roles, echo = FALSE}
roles <- gla_type()
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Role = names(roles),
  `Size (px)` = vapply(roles, function(r) r$size, numeric(1)),
  Weight = vapply(roles, function(r) r$weight, character(1)),
  For = c("The chart's title", "A supporting line beneath the title",
          "Axis names, series and legend titles", "Value labels, annotations, legend entries",
          "Axis and scale labels", "The smaller tick tier, for denser charts",
          "The footer: byline, source, note"),
  check.names = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

Sizes are in CSS pixels, as on the web, so a chart saved at 96 dpi matches a
chart drawn by the web components pixel for pixel. In points, which is what
ggplot2 measures text in, 14px is 10.5pt. `base_size` is the tick size and
the other roles scale from it.

```{r sizes}
ggplot(gla_yearly, aes(year, average, colour = series)) +
  geom_gla_line() +
  scale_colour_gla() +
  gla_labs(
    title = "The title is 20px semibold",
    subtitle = "The subtitle is 16px regular in text-muted",
    source = "The caption is 12px", x = "Axis titles are 14px medium"
  ) +
  theme_gla(axis_titles = "both")
```

## Inter

The typeface is Inter. The package bundles it (it is published under the SIL
Open Font License) and registers it with systemfonts when the package loads,
so the devices built on systemfonts draw it on any machine: ragg's `agg_png()`,
svglite, and the knitr and pkgdown output made with them. RStudio draws with
ragg when its graphics backend is set to AGG.

The base graphics devices (quartz, the Windows device, pdf) only know fonts
installed on the system. On those, `theme_gla()` falls back to the device's
sans with a bold face for the title, unless Inter is installed. `gla_font()`
says what will be used; `options(gglaplot2.font = "inter")` forces it,
`"sans"` turns it off.

```{r font}
gla_font()
gla_font("semibold")
```

The weights come as named families, because a font family in R has a plain
and a bold face and nothing between. `"Inter"` is regular with Inter Bold
as its bold; `"Inter Medium"` and `"Inter SemiBold"` are the two weights the
roles use.

## Colour and emphasis

Text colour is a separate decision from its role. The title and axis titles
are `text`, the subtitle and caption `text-muted`, tick labels
`chart-label-muted` and annotations `chart-label`. Emphasis within a role is
a change of weight, not of size.
